api.notes: The element is the handle: `focus()` and `select()` reach the inner textarea; `value` and the form API are on the host.
The `value` attribute is the default (form reset restores it); the property is the current value. In slotted-textarea mode it reads and writes the author's textarea.
Upstream onChange runs on every edit, which is the native `input` event; the native `change` fires once when the edit is committed (blur). Neither fires on property writes.
`(value, event) => void | Promise<void>` after each user edit; busy (:state(busy), aria-busy, spinner) while a returned promise is pending.
A tooltip on a disabled field that says why; the field stays focusable (aria-disabled).
The visible height in lines; with `auto-grow` it is the minimum.
A soft limit: the counter counts user-perceived characters (graphemes), typing is not stopped, and past the limit the field is aria-invalid, does not submit and the overflow is announced once.
Object `{type, message?}`, or the `status-type` and `status-message` attributes.
attached, detached or tooltip (a focusable button in the box that reveals the message).
An icon name (upstream also accepts a node; use the tct-icon element in your own content instead).

api.reason: The global `spellcheck` attribute (and property) on the host is forwarded to the inner textarea; the CEM does not list global attributes as targets (see requests).

api.notes: Composed, so it reaches the host from the inner textarea.
The global `autofocus` attribute; the element focuses its textarea once it has rendered.
Unset takes the nearest size provider, else md.
A number is px, a string a CSS length. Not reflected.

hooks.notes: Shadow mode for the field's own tree, light mode (satellites) in slotted-textarea mode.

hooks.reason: Internal render helper; the status glyph and the tooltip button are part of the element's template.

hooks.notes: The shared announcer: the counter speaks once when it nears the limit (polite) and once when it is passed (assertive).
The form layout's optionality default; the indicator follows it.

keyboard.action: Adds a line break; never submits the form.
Reaches the tooltip-variant status button, which is a real focusable button.

form.notes: Form-associated (ElementInternals): submits `name=value`, resets to the `value` attribute, restores on navigation, joins <fieldset disabled>, works with form= and label for. Validation shows after a commit, a blur after an edit or a submit attempt, never on form.checkValidity(); past `maxlength` it shows at once. Slotted-textarea mode submits the author's own <textarea> exactly once and adds no entry of its own.

differences.text: Uncontrolled by default (D-006): `value` is a property with the `value` attribute as its default, and the native `input`/`change` events report edits, instead of a controlled value plus onChange. Set the property to control it.

Slotted-textarea mode (`<textarea slot="input">`) lets browser features, autofill and form restoration see a native field; label, description and status are light-DOM satellites wired with ids. The textarea owns name, value, required, disabled, rows and autocomplete there.

`auto-grow` and `max-rows` are additions: the field grows with its text using CSS `field-sizing: content` where the browser has it (feature-detected) and a measuring fallback otherwise, clamped between `rows` and `max-rows` [mwg:form-fields-automatically-fit-contents].

Past `maxlength` the form does not submit (`validity.tooLong`), where upstream only turns the counter red. The limit stays soft: nothing is truncated while typing or pasting, and the message comes from the locale catalog.

Invalidity shows only after user interaction, on one clock: `:state(user-invalid)` and `aria-invalid` flip together, the browser's message becomes the status (announced once), and a failed submit focuses the field. Being over the limit is the one exception and shows at once, with a warning glyph beside the count.
The tooltip status variant is a focusable button with a name ("Error details", "Warning details"...) rather than a hover-only icon.

Outlined field from the Tecton input tokens (border, hover, focus ring through the shared focus-ring module, 4px element radius); the resize grip stays in the true corner because adornments and the counter are overlays.

requests.reason: The parity check should accept the global `spellcheck` attribute as a target (as it does `autofocus`), so hasSpellCheck can point at it instead of being waived.

core.text-area.notes: Guides: [mwg:form-associated-custom-elements]; [mwg:form-fields-automatically-fit-contents] field-sizing with a measured fallback; [mwg:validate-input-after-interaction]; [mwg:accessible-error-announcement] the counter and the status speak once; [mwg:required-field-feedback].
